result.rationale: The migration does interpolate raw site_settings values directly: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The site setting 'embeddable_hosts' was a free-text host_list with no validation that would have prevented a single quote, so the mechanism described (malformed SQL causing the migration to fail mid-deploy) is real and introduced by this diff. It's a correctness/data-integrity defect, though exploitation is admin-controlled input so severity is primarily the migration-crash angle.

judged_text: Host values from the free-text site_settings row are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no escaping or parameterization, so any previously configured host containing a single quote or other SQL-significant character produces a malformed statement. The migration raises a PG syntax error mid-migration (deploy blocker), aborting after the table has been created; even without quotes, the raw interpolation skips the escaping/parameterization the model layer would have applied. (Injection is Security's angle; the migration-crash data-integrity failure is this one.)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` directly interpolates each legacy host line into raw SQL: `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), this will produce invalid SQL and can abort the migration after creating the table. It also bypasses proper escaping/parameterization (and any model-layer normalization) when migrating existing data.
